-- During the search phase for a still-missing required object or tool, when you arrive at a container (drawer/cabinet/fridge) that is already open and was not opened by your immediately preceding action, treat it as already searched: do not re-examine its contents and do not re-open it.
-- Instead, move to a closed container and open it to check its contents, or to a location not observed earlier in the current search pass.
-- Do not complete or repeat a cycle back through a set of containers already observed open or empty; if the most recent observed locations are containers you have already seen open, switch to a different, not-yet-inspected location.
+- During the search phase for a still-missing required object or tool, when you arrive at a container (drawer/cabinet/fridge) that is already open and was not opened by your immediately preceding action, inspect only the contents currently shown. If the required object/tool is visible there, take it immediately instead of treating the container as searched. Otherwise, do not re-open it or linger. If the current or immediately preceding observation shows another already-open or empty container of the same furniture type, prefer a different furniture type from the admissible actions whose contents have not just been shown; otherwise move to a closed container whose contents have not yet been shown, or to a different furniture type.
+- Do not complete or repeat a cycle through containers that the current observation or the last two observation/action pairs show are already open or empty; when those recent observations show repeated containers of the same furniture type, switch to a different furniture type from the admissible actions rather than trying another container in that set.
 - This rule applies only while the required object or tool is still missing; it does not apply once you are carrying the required object and are looking for the placement receptacle.

-- During the search phase, after checking the closed containers and surfaces currently reachable, if the required object or tool is still missing, proceed to a location or furniture type that has not yet been inspected in this pass (e.g., a sidetable, dresser, coffeetable, armchair, sofa, bed, or garbagecan) rather than re-traversing locations already checked.
-- Each successive search destination should be a location that could plausibly hold the missing object/tool and has not already been observed in the current pass; do not re-enter the same limited subset of locations repeatedly.
+- During the search phase, while the required object or tool is still missing, do not return to a location or furniture type that the current observation or the last two observation/action pairs show you have just checked without finding it. When the recent observations show you are cycling among the same locations or among already-open or empty containers of one furniture type, stop that cycle and choose a different furniture type or location from the admissible actions (e.g., a sidetable, dresser, coffeetable, armchair, sofa, bed, or garbagecan) whose contents have not just been shown.
+- Otherwise continue through distinct locations, including closed containers whose contents are not currently shown; when choosing among admissible actions, prefer a location or furniture type whose contents are not shown in the current observation or the last two observation/action pairs, and do not choose another same-type container when the recent observations already show a same-type cycle. Do not re-enter the same limited subset of locations repeatedly.
 - Once the required object or tool becomes visible, stop searching: take it immediately, and then go directly to the required next location (the desklamp for examine tasks, or the destination receptacle for pick-and-place) without further search moves.
